newsitem.title: TOGO: Togo opens 96/97 coffee season, cuts farm price.
newsitem.headline: Togo opens 96/97 coffee season, cuts farm price.

text.p: Togo has opened its 1996/97 coffee marketing season and slashed its farmgate price for both arabica and robusta varieties, according to a presidential decree.
The decree, read on state television late on Thursday, said the season had begun that day with the arabica price falling to 430 CFA francs per kg of berries from 755 CFA previously.
The robusta price falls to 425 CFA from 750 CFA.
Official sources blamed the sharp cut on a fall in coffee prices on world markets.
The marketing season ends on September 30, 1997.
Togo's state marketing board OPAT predicted total output of between 16,000 and 18,000 tonnes in 1996/97. Output in 1995/96 was less than 6,000 tonnes. OPAT blamed "severe climatic conditions".
